newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 100-110 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 100-110 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall 100 billion to 110 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Thursday.
The Reuters poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 85 bcf to 130 bcf for the week ended Dec 27.
"The HDDs were pretty substantial last week, but I don't think people were very aggressive about taking it out," said a Houston trader.
In last report, overall stocks fell 130 bcf, slightly above expectations, and were 86 bcf, or 3.8 percent, below year-ago levels. The four week average drawdown is 90 bcf.

While Producing and Consuming Region West inventories continued to significantly lag 1995 levels, stocks in the critical Consuming Region East fell in the last report by 62 bcf, leaving them 143 bcf, or 11 percent, above a year ago.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped 160 bcf. A draw today in the expected range would narrow the overall gap to last year to just 30 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell 92 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 44 bcf and western stocks by 24 bcf.
